links.note: a^0 = 1 is read straight off the downward pattern 100, 10, 1, a tenth - the step past 10^1 is where 10^0 = 1 sits. No other concept in the set states the zero exponent.
Naming which of the two numbers in 10^2 is the exponent is the base/exponent vocabulary of 31438, not the repeated-multiplication computation of 31439.
10^-1 = 1/10 with base ten, exactly the reciprocal reading this concept states for 10^-2 and 10^-3.
Asks for a multiplicative inverse (10^5 -> 10^-5), which is the practice 31442 names, rather than evaluating a negative power as a fraction.
Multiplicative inverse of 10^10 is 10^-10 - the inverse-finding exercise of 31442.
(-2)^-5 x (-2)^6 = (-2)^(-5+6) = -2. Same base with one negative exponent added to one positive - the very shape of this concept's (-4)^5 x (-4)^-10 example.
(-2)^-2 = 1/(-2)^2 = 1/4. The base is not ten, so it is the any-base extension 31442 rather than 31441.
0.000007 = 7 x 10^-6 is verbatim this concept's worked example of a small number in standard form.
0.00001275 = 1.275 x 10^-5: a small number taken to standard form with a negative exponent.
2.5 x 10^4 = 25000 runs the conversion in the standard-form-to-usual-form direction that 31449 requires to work both ways.
3^2 x 4^2 = 9 x 16 = 144. Different bases, so no exponent law in this set applies; the value comes from expanding each power as repeated multiplication.
10^0 + 2^0 + 5^0 = 3 depends only on the zero exponent giving 1, which the downward pattern of this concept establishes.
(-1)^-1 = 1/(-1) = -1: a negative exponent on a base other than ten, the any-base case.
a^m x a^m = a^(2m) - same base, exponents added.
2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 written as 2^5 is precisely this concept's example of 2 multiplied by itself five times.
2^5 = 32 is evaluated by taking 2 five times - repeated multiplication.
Multiplicative inverse of 7^-2 is 7^2 = 49: base seven, and the inverse-finding practice this concept names.
All four options are small decimals, so the stem is 7 x 10^-5 (the minus was lost in extraction) and the key 0.00007 is right; the work is standard form back to usual form.
1^15 = 1 by taking the base 15 times, the m-fold repeated multiplication of this concept.
3^5 = 243 by repeated multiplication of the base.
Duplicate of qid 113791: (-2)^-2 = 1/4, a negative exponent on a non-ten base.
a^m divided by a^n = a^(m-n) - the division law that subtracts exponents.
5^3 x 5^-1 = 5^(3-1) = 25: one multiplication, same base, exponents added with a sign.
3^2 x 3^-4 x 3^5 = 3^(2-4+5) = 27. Three factors of one base, the signed exponents simply summed.
(1/2)^-4 = 2^4 = 16: a negative exponent turned into a reciprocal on a fractional base, the any-base case.
149600000000 written as 1.496 x 10^11 - the usual-form-to-standard-form direction of the conversion.
300000000 written as 3 x 10^8: a large number taken into standard form.
695000 written as 6.95 x 10^5 - converting a given number to standard form.
1 micron is one millionth of a metre, i.e. 1/10^6 = 10^-6 m - the same one-over-a-million-to-negative-exponent step this concept sets out.
140,000,000,000 kg expressed as 1.4 x 10^11 kg: a given number written in standard form.
Duplicate of qid 113788 - multiplicative inverse of 10^5, the inverse-finding practice.
a^m x a^n = a^(m+n) stated as a law: same base, exponents added.
